short: A pious but ineffective King of England whose weak rule triggered the Wars of the Roses.
full:
Inheriting the English throne at the age of nine months on 1 September 1422, Henry VI grew into a peaceful, deeply religious man ill-suited to the violent politics of his era. His reign saw the loss of almost all English territories in France and severe domestic factionalism.

Henry suffered a catastrophic mental breakdown in 1453, creating a power vacuum that led directly to civil war. He was deposed in 1461, briefly restored as a puppet monarch in 1470, and finally deposed again. He died in the Tower of London shortly after the Battle of Tewkesbury, almost certainly murdered on the orders of Edward IV.
